narrative.intro: Applied Research Solutions has $242M in federal contract obligations for FY2026 to date. Applied Research Solutions won 7 awards this fiscal year, with an average award size of $34.5M, and obligations are down 9.4% year over year. Applied Research Solutions receives most business from the Department of Defense, which obligated $235M, followed by the General Services Administration with $6.4M. Applied Research Solutions sells primarily research and development services: Research and Development in the Physical, Engineering, and Life Sciences (except Biotechnology) accounts for $223M and Research and Development in the Physical, Engineering, and Life Sciences (except Nanotechnology and Biotechnology) accounts for $11.9M. Applied Research Solutions also has $6.4M in Engineering Services and $921K in Process, Physical Distribution, and Logistics Consulting Services. Applied Research Solutions obligations have varied by fiscal year: FY21 $207M, FY22 $213M, FY23 $238M, FY24 $208M, FY25 $267M, and FY26 $242M.

sections.heading: How concentrated are Applied Research Solutions federal obligations?
sections.body: The Department of Defense is the dominant buyer for Applied Research Solutions, accounting for $235M of FY2026 to date obligations. The General Services Administration is a distant second with $6.4M. The Research and Development NAICS categories together represent the largest share of Applied Research Solutions obligations, led by a $223M category.

sections.heading: How have Applied Research Solutions obligations trended recently?
sections.body: Applied Research Solutions obligations rose from FY21 $207M to FY25 $267M before falling to FY26 $242M. Applied Research Solutions obligations are down 9.4% year over year in FY2026 to date compared with the prior year.

faq.q: Which agencies buy from Applied Research Solutions?

Applied Research Solutions has $223M in Research and Development in the Physical, Engineering, and Life Sciences (except Biotechnology), $11.9M in Research and Development in the Physical, Engineering, and Life Sciences (except Nanotechnology and Biotechnology), $6.4M in Engineering Services, and $921K in Process, Physical Distribution, and Logistics Consulting Services.
